name: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, Ibn Ulayyah
nameAr: إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن مقسم الأسدي مولاهم، أبو بشر، البصري، المعروف بابن علية

laqab.en: Ibn Ulayyah: Ulayyah was his mother (al-Khatib records a claim that she was his grandmother)

verdicts.via: Ali ibn al-Ja'd; Yunus ibn Bukayr
verdicts.ar: إسماعيل ابن علية ريحانة الفقهاء … ابن علية سيد المحدثين
verdicts.en: Isma'il ibn Ulayyah is the fragrant flower of the jurists; Ibn Ulayyah is the master of the hadith scholars.
With him ends the line of verification in Basra.

verdicts.ar: ما أقول إن أحدا أثبت في الحديث من ابن علية
verdicts.en: I do not say that anyone is firmer in hadith than Ibn Ulayyah.

flags.label: Attributed to his mother
flags.detail: Ibn Hajar lists him in Hady al-Sari among those referred to by other than the father's name: “Ibn Ulayyah: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Miqsam; Ulayyah is his mother, or, it is said, his grandmother.” Al-Bukhari writes “Ibn Ulayyah” in hadith 15; Muslim 44a writes “Isma'il ibn Ulayyah”.

bio: The Basran whom Ahmad named the end-point of verification in his city and Ibn al-Madini ranked second to none in precision; a client of Banu Asad known by his mother's name. He served over the alms of Basra and later over grievances in Baghdad. In hadith 15 he carries Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb's version, whose wording in Muslim differs from the Qatadah wording al-Bukhari printed.

provenance.ref: Hady al-Sari, ch. 7, those mentioned by the name of a father, grandfather or the like

sources.label: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 7: those referred to by a father's or other relative's name (Wikisource)
